source.title: Comparing Physician and Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Patient Questions Posted to a Public Social Media Forum

confidence_rationale: Direct, high-visibility demonstration in an actual artificial system that concern-shaped linguistic output can be produced with no affective or other-model architecture whatsoever and rated as MORE empathetic than trained human clinicians by an expert language-only judging panel. This is the masking hazard of Q-091 realised, not analogised: a licensed-professional panel preferred ChatGPT responses ~79% of the time and rated them higher on 'empathy or bedside manner'. Source quality is high (JAMA Internal Medicine, pre-registered cross-sectional design, triplicate rating). Held at 0.7 because the study measures RATED empathy of text, not whether an underlying empathic architecture exists -- it demonstrates that a language-only evaluation is foolable, which is Q-091's premise, but does not by itself validate the specific non-linguistic probe Q-091 seeks.
failure_signatures: A panel of licensed healthcare professionals rated a system with categorically no affective or other-model architecture (an LLM) as MORE empathetic than human physicians and preferred its responses ~79% of the time -- a language-only evaluation inverted the true ordering of empathic capacity.

The authors note ChatGPT tended to produce longer responses, which raters may erroneously associate with greater empathy -- a concrete surface-feature confound showing how easily a linguistic judge is captured by form rather than by any underlying caring state.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a cross-sectional study of 195 physician-answered questions from Reddit's r/AskDocs, a panel of licensed health-care professionals, blinded and rating anonymised randomly-ordered responses in triplicate, preferred ChatGPT's responses to physicians' in ~79% of evaluations and rated the chatbot's responses significantly higher on both quality of information and on 'empathy or bedside manner'.
mapping.ree_translation: This is a live instance of the exact evaluation failure Q-091 warns about: a system with no other-model and no affective-relevance architecture produced concern-shaped language that expert judges scored as more empathetic than humans who (presumably) possess that architecture. It confirms that an evaluation which reads empathy off linguistic output cannot discriminate a fluent-but-empathy-less system from an empathic one -- so REE's evaluation of caring commitment must not rest on judged linguistic concern, and must instead use a probe (costly other-directed action, residue after exploiting a cooperating other) that a language-only imitator cannot pass.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The study measures human raters' PERCEIVED empathy of physician vs chatbot text; it does not measure or claim anything about the presence of an internal empathic state in either party, nor does it test a non-linguistic discriminating probe. It shows the language-only judge is foolable (Q-091's premise) but does not itself establish the fix. Domain transfer from clinical Q&A text to an REE V4 caring-commitment substrate is substantial.
mapping.source_context: Cross-sectional study, 195 anonymised public medical Q&A exchanges, blinded triplicate ratings by licensed clinicians; text-only comparison of a general-purpose LLM (ChatGPT) against verified physicians.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (JAMA IM, blinded triplicate design). Mapping fidelity good for the PREMISE (language-only evaluation is foolable, demonstrated in a real artificial system) but only indirect for the ANSWER Q-091 seeks (a validated non-linguistic probe). Transfer risk elevated: clinical Q&A text is far from an REE caring-commitment setting, and 'rated empathy' is a perception measure, not an architecture measure.
